title: Work can look stable in hours while care and housing position narrow household room
source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled comparison of 2025 SIPP person-month directional transitions, tenure/care distributions, and stable-SNAP child-care/hardship pairs

observations.period: 2024 reference year; month-t resource band to month-t+1 earnings/hours direction

denominator.unit: valid earnings person-month pairs in work-limiting cells; hours direction uses a separate 11,548-pair universe

work_limited_below_1x_earnings_direction.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 2.938, 2.447, and 4.934 percentage points

work_limited_below_1x_hours_direction.unit: percent; Fay-BRR SE 1.685, 1.450, and 2.547 percentage points

observations.method: Same-person SIPP monthly cross-lag using THINCPOV at month t and directional TPEARN/TMWKHRS at month t+1, conditioned on EDISABL, WPFINWGT, and 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights with perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: Earnings and hours use separate valid pair universes. Directional movement is descriptive and does not identify desired hours, job quality, accommodation, care response, or causality.
observations.subgroup: Reported work-limiting condition, stratified by four resource bands; comparison to non-limiting cells remains in the source record.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher-resource respondents can show more earnings movement in both directions because earnings have more room to move or because job composition differs. Stable hours do not prove stable welfare.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; child-care payment/help/work prevention by tenure and income-to-poverty band

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; each care measure has its own official conditional universe

payment_help_pattern.value: help paying is higher in lower-income renter and owner cells than in the displayed 4x+ cells

observations.method: Person-weighted SIPP tenure × monthly income-to-poverty diagnostic using official child-care field universes, status flags, WPFINWGT, and 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: This is a person-record distribution rather than an official household prevalence estimate. Tenure, income, payment, help, and work-prevention fields have different valid universes; the association is not causal.
observations.subgroup: ETENURE owner/buyer versus renter, crossed with four income-to-poverty bands; reference-parent child-care fields.
observations.counterinterpretation: Tenure may proxy for resources, stability, place, provider reach, family composition, or schedule flexibility; the screen does not identify which mechanism matters.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; stable SNAP November–December pairs conditioned on fall child-care work prevention

denominator.unit: valid stable-SNAP person pairs across the 328 no-prevention and 23 prevention cells; hardship outcomes have separate valid universes

observations.method: Same-person November–December stable-SNAP pair with annual fall child-care work-prevention status attached to the following-month hardship outcome; 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: The stable-SNAP prevention cell has 23 valid pairs and wide intervals. Annual care timing is not a dated episode, and the contrast is not causal.
observations.subgroup: Reference parents in stable SNAP-status pairs, split by child-care work prevention; stable no-SNAP comparison retained as a counter-surface.
observations.counterinterpretation: Household composition, income, employment, eligibility, care need, prior hardship, and unmeasured shocks may explain both prevention and later hardship.

related_sources.claim: The directional SIPP finding supplies the monthly earnings/hours result and its boundary.
The tenure × poverty layer supplies the child-care payment, help, and work-prevention comparison.
The stable-SNAP bridge supplies following-month hardship comparisons and small-cell uncertainty.

boundary: This is a deliberately non-pooled SIPP synthesis. It connects directional work movement, tenure/care distributions, and a stable-SNAP following-hardship bridge without treating them as one household estimate. It does not establish a care, tenure, SNAP, hardship, earnings, or hours causal effect; the next conditional person-month rerun requires the raw SIPP slice and replicate archive. Recovery, trust, political action, and institutional remedy remain open.
